items.title: The localisation S^{-1}A is the zero ring exactly when 0 lies in S
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the collapse of a localisation: S^{-1}A is the zero ring if and only if 0 lies in S (statement lines 1327-1330). Both directions are settled directly from the equivalence relation that defines the localisation, without any computation with the ring structure: with 0 in S every pair (a, s) is equivalent to (0, 1), and with 0 outside S the two classes 1/1 and 0/1 stay distinct (proof lines 1332-1335). The content is recognising that the collapse condition is exactly membership of 0 in the multiplicative subset, which is the kind of step a reader must supply; the author states both directions in full. H2.
